N Ay Rapier, come foorth, come forth I ſay, Ile giue thee a crowne, though it be but a crackt one: what wilt not? art ſo hard to be drawne forth Rapier? Yes if youle be ſingle Rapier too. Ile tell you what, if I goe into the Field with him, hang Sword vp if I doe not cut Rapiers poynts, and laſh him when I haue done: nay, you ſhall finde Sword mettle to the very backe: 'sfoot, my teeth be an edge at him. Hang him, I defie him baſe Spa niard. Capon? Well Rapier, if thou goeſt into the fields with me, Ile make a Capon of you before I haue done with you, you ſhall nere come home vncut Ile warrant you. Nere talke you of hacking, for it's a hundred to one if you haue not the Foyle-Rapier. The Cutler, Alas wee are the beſt Friends hee has, and if it were not for vs, the Cutler might ſoone ſhut vp his ſhoppe. But it were more wiſedome then to ſtand: For the Cutler is a man as well Ar med as any man I knowe, and has as good skill ins weapons. Syr, Sword has bene proou'd be fore now, and yet heele prooue himſelfe a gaine with you, if you dare follow him. What talke you of Law? Sword ſcornes to haue any other Law then Martiall law, and that vpon you Rapier. Why Sir, tis well knowne that Sword has flouriſht in his dayes. I hope knows how to keep his quarters Rapier a Gentleman? No, no, its Sworde that's the no table Souldier; Why, theres none of all you Captaines could doe anie thing in Warre without him. Yet hees not fit for a Souldier, any man may bende him as hee liſt. Then let mee alone to tickle Bowes ownes nocke yfaith. Bill, Ile pay him ſoundly, if ere I reach him. Its' nere but when Powder ouer charges him, then indeed heel be ſomewhat hote oth matter. I wonder they ſhould chuſe him: Why he does euery thing on the ſudden. I but hees No-body now-adayes, Hees blovvne vp long agoe. Dare I? You ſhall ſoone ſee that: Goe, and Ile follovv you. Why, you are a backe-Friend to vs both Dagger.
S'foot thou ſhalt know that Rapier dares enter: nay Backe-Sword. Whoſe this behinde me? Well Sword, Dagger hath defen ded you a good many times; but tis no mat ter, another time ſhall ſerue: ſhall I get you out Sword alone, that I may haue you Single-ſword. I Capon, ſo I ſay ſir. He a Cutter? alas he nere went into the fields yet, but he was ſoundly hackt before he came out 'Sfoot if you be ſo Short-Sword, Rapier nere feares you: come a long. Better for mee? Alas hee knewe not how to vſe mee. Yet I ſcorne to runne away from him. Ha Sworde, is the winde in that Doore? Faith nowe I ſee which waye you ſtand bent Sworde, you had rather ſleepe in a whole skinne, then goe into the Fields to trye your ſelfe. Syr, wee will fight, and doe you take it in Dudgeon Dagger if you pleaſe: if you once offer to hinder vs, Ile ſo Pummell you Dagger, that you were neuer better Pummeld in your life; And howſoeuer, I hope theres Lawe againſt you as well as o thers, and Rapier can put vp a Caſe againſt you. I, you doe well, to excuſe his Cowardiſe. With Scarffes? with a Halter, if he had beene well ſeru'de, For hees a nota ble Theefe. I, a Thiefe. Did you nere heare of Cutting-Dicke, this is the very ſame man. Sword beare Armes? Hees a baſe companion. Alas I haue knowne you beare a Basket Sword. I, the draggon in Suſſex, the other day: But Ile warrant you Rapiers of as good a blood as hee for his hart. And oftentimes the younger bro ther prooues the better Souldier. I hope Rapier hath not beene at Fencing-Schoole all this while for nothing. Indeed they ſay that Bow has bin an olde Souldier. And as for Bow-ſtring, I dare vn dertake to whip him my ſelfe. Gunne, Alas hees No-body: any little Boy will make him roare. I haue made him goe off 'oth Fieldes, a good many times my ſelfe. I think that Powder is a vile brag ger, he doth nothing but cracke. Hee a Parlement-man: For what Shyre? Nay, you ſhould let him alone Dagger, and you ſhould ſee that Swords' as notable a bragger as Povvder. He thinks hee ſhall nere be matcht too: but hee ſhall, and ouer-matcht too, by Rapier; I vvarrant him. Come Sworde, after your long Parley, Dare you goe into the Fieldes? Nay let him chooſe, Rapiers at a good poynt, whether he will or no. Wee are. A Long-Sword.
Tis Dagger ſir; what will you neuer leaue your quarrelling? Nay, you ſhall finde Sword a notable Cutter. Nay nere goe, for if you doe, Ile ſende one after you, which ſhall ſcowre you both. The Cutler can doe it. I haue ſeene him handle you both brauely. Alas Sword, you need not talke of his ſhutting vp of Shoppe, and if it had not beene for him, you had broken by this time Sword, Nay, nere talke: For you know hee can holde your noſe to the Grind-ſtone, when hee liſt. And as for you Rapier, you knowe hee brought you vp firſt, and if you had ſtayed with him ſtill, it might haue bene better for you. Hee vſde you too well indeede: for when you were with him he furniſht you with Siler and euery thing, but now you are worne out of all faſhion. You are euen like a Lapwing, you are no ſooner Hatcht Ra pier, but you runne abroade preſently from him. Doe you heare Sworde? If you goe, looke for Dagger at your backs preſent lie; For I am a Iuſtice of Peace, and am ſworne to keepe and defend the Peace. Alas I care not if you were both Plaintifes againſt mee, you ſhall finde Dag ger your Defendant Ile warrant you: I, and if neede bee, I could put vp an Action of Batterie againſt you. Away Sworde, the Time was in deed when thou waſt a notable Swaſh-buck ler, but now thou art growne olde Sword. Flouriſht? yfaith Syr I, I haue ſeene Sword hang with nothing but Scarffes ere now. A Theefe? Nay Rapier, nere hit Sword ith teeth with that: for you know you were both Indited for treaſon before now, and were in danger to be hangd, and drawn too, and had eſcapt well if you had not bene quarterd. You are a craftie Foxe Sword: It were well if you knewe howe to keepe your friendſhip too, for Gentlemen and Friendes ſhould not fall out. Nay, Dagger will defende you both for good Souldiers. Yes Rapier is a Souldier, and a Man as well Armed at all poyntes as anie one. Alas there's none Maiſter of De fence but Dagger: But yet if you ſpeake of Souldiers, the'rs Bow, Bill, and Gunne, worth twenty ſuch as wee are. But what ſay you to Bill? hees a notable ſturdy villaine. Its more then you can doe, Ime affraide; For Bill's a Tall-fellow ons hands, and will quickly be Wood: and then theres Gunne, ſuch another Bouncing-fellow too. Well, is Gunne No-bodie? Ime ſure heel giue ſome blowes ſometimes. Faith I knowe not what Souldi er hee is, but they ſay, Hees an excellent pol litician. Why, hee has an excellent wit? Ime ſure I can remember ſince he was a Parlement-man. Well, if eyther you, or any body elſe ſhuld meete with Povvder, yet its a hun dred to one, if he meete not vvith his match. Nay, you knowe Ime equally al lyed to you both, and therefore ſhall proue an impartiall Iudge: How ſay you, will you be rulde by me? Why are are you ſo long Sword before you ſpeake? Then in briefe it ſhall bee thus. Sworde, you ſhall beare Chiefe force ith Campe, and be made Generall of the Field, to beare ſway euery where. As for you Ra pier, ſince Duells are put downe, you ſhall liue quietly and peaceablie heere 'ith Court, and goe euery day in Veluet: You ſhall be Frendes with euerie one, and bee on euery ones ſide, that if occaſion ſerue, and Sworde be abſent, ſo that matters are driue ̄ to a puſh, Rapier ſhall be the onely man to performe a Combate: And I my ſelfe will backe you both, as occaſion ſhall ſerue. How ſay yee, are yee content? Then goe before to my Houſe, to the Dagger in Cheape: and there weele conclude all. Our weapons drawne, and yet no hurt yee finde, Did Dagger then defend vnto your minde? Hee that defended others not long ſence, At laſt hee dares not ſtand ins owne defence; But this hee hopes, with you it will ſuffize, To craue a pardon for a Schollers Prize.
Nay Sword, put the Caſe of Rapiers aſide, that there were two of them, I hope you were able to buckle with them. If you offer but to thruſt towards him Rapier, Ile ſtrike you downe. But mee thinkes Sworde by the very ſounding of his Name ſhould bee the better Gentleman, and has the better Armes too: for if the truth were well knowne, Rapier hath but one arme. If you looke ith booke of Armorie, Ile warrant you, you ſhall finde Sworde of more antiquitie then you Rapier: Hee deriues his Pedigree from Morglay, Beuis of South-hamp tons ſword; and that from S. George his ſword, that killd the Draggon. Byth maſſe, I thinke indeed, you are both wel ſanguind. Your both of one blood, only thers this difference, that ſword coms of the elder brother, & you Rapier of the yo ̄ ger. Nay ber-lady, it was for the whole Countrey. Oh he plottes ſhrevvdly. If they had not look't too it, Hee had vndermined the vvhole parlement-houſe. Well ſaide, deſperate Dicke. Sword, You may be aſham'd to offer it. You knovve you are tvvo-handed- Sworde, and Rapier has but one hand (vnleſſe I helpe him) to do any good vvithall, and yet youde haue him go in to the Fieldes vvith you. Come, theres ney ther of you ſhall goe. Doe not you knovve that Duells are put downe? Youle bee bound to'th Peace euer heere-after, if you ſtrike but one ſtroke. Therefore you had beſt let me decide your controuerſie for you.
Defie me? ſirrha Sword, Rapier ſpits i'thy face: dar'ſt meete mee i'the fields, cra uenly Capon? A Gentleman? and has Armes.
Why any man may ſee that thou art well caru'd Sword; and yet mee thinks that Rapier ſhould not ſpeake of that, for it's an hundred to one if he be not gilt too.
Rapier a Souldier? When did you ere knowe Rapier fight a Battell? Are duells put downe? Then I am forc'de to be Friends: Speake then.
speeches.Sword,: Piſh, Its nothing but a flaſh.
